features.status: Track the status of each issuance.

what.a: Corvo is an API platform for issuing and managing electronic service tax invoices (NFS-e). It lets you integrate invoice issuance into your own system.

free.q: Can I use Corvo for free?
free.a: Yes. Free includes one company and up to 15 authorized production invoices per month, with a limit of 3 per day. The allowance renews on the first day of the month and limits use UTC. No credit card is required; test invoices do not consume this allowance.

multiCompany.a: Yes. Paid plans allow managing multiple issuer companies, according to each subscription's limits.

accumulate.a: No. Unused allowance does not roll over. Free renews on the first day of each month in UTC; paid plans follow the monthly subscription period shown in the dashboard.

email.q: Can I send the invoice by email?
email.a: Yes. You can request XML and PDF delivery to the customer’s email once the invoice is authorized and documents are available. Track delivery status in the Service.

storage.a: Yes. Corvo stores issuance records and available XML and PDF documents, with permission-based access. Retention follows the Terms of Service and Privacy Notice. Download copies to meet your company’s retention obligations.

nfeProducts.q: Does Corvo issue NF-e for products?
nfeProducts.a: At this time, the product focuses on NFS-e, for service provision. There is no support for NF-e for goods or NFC-e.

coverage.q: Does Corvo work in all municipalities?
coverage.a: Availability depends on the integrations and requirements applicable to the municipality and the issuer company. Check available coverage before starting the integration.

developer.q: Do I need to be a developer to use it?
developer.a: The API was designed for software integration. Corvo also offers an interface for document management and queries.

accountant.a: No. Corvo provides technological infrastructure for issuing tax documents. Tax classification and accounting obligations remain the responsibility of the company, with support from appropriate professionals.

Terms.title: Terms of Service

s1.title: 1. Acceptance and company identification
s1.content: These Terms govern your use of the Corvo dashboard, API, documentation and related services (the Service), operated by Greenflow Desenvolvimento de Software LTDA, CNPJ 61.469.487/0001-40 (Greenflow or Corvo). By creating an account or using the Service, you accept these Terms. If you act for an organization, you must be authorized to represent it. A separately signed enterprise agreement prevails where it conflicts with these Terms.

s2.title: 2. What the Service provides
s2.content: Corvo lets you integrate the issuance and management of Brazilian electronic service invoices (NFS-e) into your software. The Service includes issuer company registration, certificate management, status tracking, access to XML and PDF when available, document delivery by email and webhooks. Issuance is asynchronous: confirmation that a request was submitted does not mean the invoice was authorized. Check the result through the API, dashboard or webhooks. The test environment produces documents with no fiscal validity and does not consume the production allowance. The current scope is NFS-e; goods invoices (NF-e) and consumer invoices (NFC-e) are not included.

s3.title: 3. Account, workspace and access
s3.content: Keep account and workspace information accurate and current. You must control workspace access, assign appropriate permissions and protect your email, sessions, API keys and webhook secrets. Do not expose credentials in browser applications or public repositories. Notify Corvo of suspected unauthorized access. You are responsible for authorized use of your account, without excluding Greenflow’s responsibility for failures attributable to it.

s4.title: 4. Fiscal responsibilities
s4.content: You must be authorized to issue invoices for registered companies and verify issuer, customer, service, amount, tax, fiscal code, tax regime and municipality information. You must meet registration, accreditation and eligibility requirements imposed by the tax authority and track authorizations, rejections and pending requests. Corvo provides integration technology; fiscal and accounting decisions must be checked with the professionals responsible. A rejection, outage or test document does not replace your fiscal obligations.

s5.title: 5. Digital certificates
s5.content: Where an integration requires an A1 digital certificate, upload only a valid certificate belonging to the issuer company or a representative authorized for the operation. By uploading it, you authorize its use, together with the supplied password, to sign and transmit the fiscal operations you request through the Service. Keep the certificate valid and replace it when needed. Deactivating a certificate in Corvo prevents its further use in the Service; you must request revocation with the issuing certification authority separately.

s6.title: 6. Acceptable use and abuse prevention
s6.content: Do not use the Service to issue false documents, act without company authorization, commit fraud, send spam, distribute unlawful content or violate third-party rights. Do not bypass allowances, company limits, request limits, access controls or Free plan eligibility rules, including through accounts or workspaces created for that purpose. Do not share API access beyond your contracted permissions or interfere with the Service or connected fiscal systems.

s7.title: 7. Plans, allowances and renewal
s7.content: Plans define the monthly invoice allowance, active company limit and usage limits shown in the offer and dashboard. Free allows one active company and up to 15 authorized production invoices per month, with a limit of 3 per day. Its allowance renews on the first day of each month; monthly and daily limits use UTC. Paid allowances follow the monthly subscription period shown in the dashboard. Allowances belong to the workspace, not to each member or API key. Unused allowance does not roll over or convert into cash. Once a limit is reached, new requests may be blocked until renewal or the purchase of appropriate capacity.

s8.title: 8. How usage and overage are calculated
s8.content: Each authorized production NFS-e counts as one usage unit. Corvo reserves capacity when it receives a request while issuance is in progress. Rejected invoices and invoices that finish with a failure release that reservation; invoices still processing may temporarily reduce available capacity. If authorization completes after renewal, usage stays in the period in which it was reserved. Free does not allow paid overage. On paid plans, authorized invoices above the allowance incur additional charges at the plan’s unit rate, within a total monthly processing limit of five times the included allowance. Check usage, reservations and estimated overage in the dashboard.

s9.title: 9. Billing, plan changes and cancellation
s9.content: Paid subscriptions are monthly, in Brazilian reais, and renew automatically until canceled. The base fee is charged at the start of the cycle and overage is charged after use; late authorizations may result in a later charge for the original period. Stripe processes payments, and activation requires payment confirmation. The current offer does not include annual subscriptions or prepaid packs. Plan changes and cancellation to return to Free take effect at the end of the current period, without immediate proration of the base fee. Use the subscription options and billing portal in the dashboard; stopping account use does not cancel a subscription. After a failed renewal, paid issuance may remain available for up to seven days after the paid period ends, depending on subscription status, and may then be blocked. Cancellation does not remove charges for usage already incurred. Send refund requests or billing disputes to the contact in these Terms; mandatory statutory rights remain protected, including withdrawal rights where applicable.

s10.title: 10. Fiscal documents and retention
s10.content: Corvo stores issuance records and the XML and PDF documents it generates or receives, making them available according to invoice status and your access permissions. Document generation or retrieval failures may require further processing. Storage in the Service does not promise indefinite retention or a specific fiscal retention period unless expressly agreed in a separate contract. Keep your own copies and download documents while you have access to the Service. You remain responsible for retaining documents for the period required for your activity. Export, access or deletion requests after termination are handled under the Privacy Notice, legal obligations and contracted conditions.

s11.title: 11. Coverage and third-party services
s11.content: Issuance depends on integration coverage, company eligibility, valid certificates and the availability of the national or municipal fiscal systems involved. Verify compatibility before operating in production. Corvo also uses infrastructure, storage, email and payment providers. External systems may delay, reject or interrupt operations. Sending an email or webhook does not guarantee receipt at the destination; track status and configure your integration to query results and handle failures. These dependencies do not exclude Greenflow’s statutory responsibilities for its own actions.

s12.title: 12. Personal data and privacy
s12.content: For customer, issuer, fiscal document and instruction data submitted to the Service, Greenflow acts as a processor on the customer’s behalf under documented instructions and the Data Processing Addendum. The customer must have a lawful basis, inform data subjects and be authorized by the controller when acting on its behalf. Greenflow acts as controller for data needed to manage accounts, billing, security and support. The Privacy Notice and Data Processing Addendum supplement these Terms. Both parties must comply with Brazil’s LGPD and other applicable rules.

s13.title: 13. Security
s13.content: Corvo uses access controls, workspace and environment data separation, API-key hashes, encryption of stored certificates and signed webhooks. You must protect credentials, review permissions and verify signatures received by your integration. No system is entirely free of risk. Specific audit, certification, data location or service-level commitments require an express agreement; they do not arise solely from using the Service.

s14.title: 14. Suspension and termination
s14.content: We may restrict or suspend access where there are reasonable indications of fraud, unauthorized issuance, security risk, breach of these Terms or nonpayment preventing use of the plan. Where possible, we will explain the reason and how to resolve it. You may request account closure through the contact in these Terms and must manage subscription cancellation in the dashboard. Closure does not cancel an NFS-e already authorized by the tax authority or extinguish payment or document retention obligations already incurred.

s15.content: Data and documents you submit remain under your responsibility and are not transferred to Greenflow by these Terms. You authorize the processing needed to provide the Service and execute your instructions. Greenflow retains rights in Corvo’s software, brand and documentation, subject to third-party rights. While complying with these Terms, you may use the Service and documentation for your contracted integrations.

Also to the extent permitted by law, Greenflow is not liable for indirect damages or lost profits. These limits do not exclude liabilities that cannot be limited, mandatory consumer rights or duties under data-protection law.

s18.content: These Terms are governed by Brazilian law. The parties will seek to resolve questions and disputes through the contact below. For unresolved disputes, the courts of the District of Ourinhos, State of São Paulo, have jurisdiction, subject to mandatory jurisdiction rules and the consumer’s right to use the legally applicable forum.

Privacy.title: Privacy Notice
Privacy.description: How Corvo processes account data, fiscal documents, certificates and personal data when issuing NFS-e.

s1.title: 1. Who operates the Service
s1.content: Corvo is operated by Greenflow Desenvolvimento de Software LTDA, CNPJ 61.469.487/0001-40. This Notice explains personal data processing on the website, dashboard and NFS-e issuance and management API. The Data Processing Addendum also applies to data customers submit in their fiscal operations.

s2.title: 2. Data processed
s2.content: We process account and workspace data, such as names, email addresses, members and permissions; issuer and customer data, such as CPF or CNPJ tax identifiers, municipal registration, names, addresses and contact details; and fiscal data, such as service descriptions, amounts, taxes, service dates, identifiers, statuses, XML and PDF. We also process digital certificates and their passwords when submitted for issuance, webhook configurations and deliveries, authentication and access records, billing information and support communications. Submit only data needed for the operation; avoid including sensitive personal data in service descriptions.

s3.title: 3. Purposes and legal bases
s3.content: We use data to authenticate users, administer accounts, process issuance, sign documents when authorized, store and provide XML and PDF, send emails and webhooks, process payments and provide support. We also process data to protect the Service, prevent fraud and meet legal obligations. Where we act as controller, legal bases include contract performance, legal obligations, the exercise of rights and legitimate interests, depending on the purpose and data-subject rights. We use consent for optional website analytics. Where we act as processor, we follow the customer’s documented instructions.

s4.title: 4. Customer and Greenflow roles
s4.content: The customer determines the purposes and lawful basis for fiscal data it submits, acting as controller or an authorized representative of a controller. Greenflow processes that data as processor to execute instructions and provide the Service. Greenflow acts as controller for account administration, billing, security and support. If a data-subject request concerns a customer’s fiscal data, we may refer it to the responsible party for assessment and provide appropriate assistance.

s5.title: 5. Sharing
s5.content: We share necessary data with fiscal systems involved in issuance, including the competent tax authority, and with hosting, storage, email, payment, monitoring and support providers. Sending an invoice by email shares the documents with the address designated by the customer; webhooks send events to the configured destination. Stripe processes payments through Checkout and the billing portal; Corvo receives identifiers, statuses and records needed for the subscription without collecting the full card number through its own form. We may also share data to meet legal obligations. We do not sell personal data.

s6.title: 6. Cookies and browser storage
s6.content: We use session cookies for authentication and browser storage for language, fiscal environment and cookie preferences. When configured, Google Analytics loads on the public website after cookie acceptance and does not load on login or dashboard routes. It helps analyze navigation and traffic. You can remove cookies and the saved preference in browser settings to choose again on a later visit. Restricting necessary cookies may prevent login or features from working.

s7.title: 7. International transfers
s7.content: Service providers may process data outside Brazil. International transfers must follow the mechanisms and safeguards required by the LGPD and applicable regulations, including standard contractual clauses where that mechanism is used. This Notice does not promise exclusive hosting in a specific country. You may request information about providers and transfers through the contact below.

s8.title: 8. Storage and retention
s8.content: We store fiscal documents and records needed for operations. Retention depends on the data category, purpose, contractual relationship and applicable legal obligations; we do not promise automatic deletion after 90 days or indefinite storage. Data may be retained after termination where there is a lawful basis, with access restricted to the retention purpose. Access, export and deletion requests are assessed under the LGPD, contract and retention obligations. Keep your own copies of documents needed for your activity.

s9.title: 9. Security measures
s9.content: We use access controls and separate data by workspace and environment. API keys are verified using one-way hashes. Digital certificates and passwords stored with them are encrypted; webhook events are signed so recipients can verify them. These measures reduce risk, but no system is completely secure. Protect credentials and report suspected unauthorized access.

s10.title: 10. Data-subject rights
s10.content: Where provided by law, you may request confirmation of processing, access, correction, sharing information, portability and anonymization, blocking or deletion of unnecessary, excessive or unlawfully processed data. You may also withdraw consent, request deletion of data processed with consent subject to lawful retention exceptions, and complain to the competent authority. Send requests to the contact below. We may request proportionate information to verify your identity and authority before responding.

s11.title: 11. Contact
s11.content: For personal data requests and questions, email legal@corvo.tech. Correspondence address: Greenflow Desenvolvimento de Software LTDA, Rua Doutor Arlindo Luz, 540, Sala 01, Centro, Ourinhos, São Paulo, postal code 19900-011, Brazil. Describe your relationship with the account or issuer company; do not send passwords or certificate files to this contact.

s12.title: 12. Notice updates
s12.content: We may update this Notice to reflect changes to the Service and data processing. The date at the top identifies the latest update. We will communicate relevant changes through Service channels where applicable. Changes requiring new consent are not authorized solely by continued use.

Dpa.title: Data Processing Addendum
Dpa.description: Customer and Greenflow responsibilities for processing personal data to issue and manage NFS-e.

s1.title: 1. Scope and relationship with the Terms
s1.content: This Addendum forms part of the Terms of Service where Greenflow Desenvolvimento de Software LTDA, CNPJ 61.469.487/0001-40, processes personal data on the customer’s behalf through Corvo. It covers processing needed to issue and manage NFS-e. For that processing, this Addendum prevails over conflicting general Terms. Data Greenflow processes as an independent controller is described in the Privacy Notice.

s2.title: 2. Roles and instructions
s2.content: The customer acts as controller or represents that the controller has authorized it to provide data and instructions. Greenflow acts as processor and processes data to provide, protect and support the Service under the contract, workspace settings and lawful documented instructions. If an instruction appears incompatible with data-protection law, Greenflow will notify the customer and may suspend the affected operation while the issue is clarified.

s3.title: 3. Data categories and subjects
s3.content: Processing may involve workspace representatives and members, service providers and customers, contacts and other people identified in fiscal documents. Data includes names, CPF or CNPJ tax identifiers, registrations, addresses, emails, service descriptions, amounts, taxes, fiscal identifiers and statuses, XML, PDF, webhook configurations and events and operational records. Certificates and passwords submitted for signing are also processed to execute authorized operations. Customers must limit submissions to necessary data and avoid sensitive personal data without an appropriate need and lawful basis.

s4.title: 4. Purpose, operations and duration
s4.content: Operations include receipt, validation, signing, transmission to fiscal systems, result queries, document storage and access, delivery by email and webhook and operational support. Processing continues during the Service and afterwards only while there is a lawful basis for retention or to complete applicable return or deletion. Test environment data should be fictitious wherever possible.

s5.title: 5. Customer duties
s5.content: The customer is responsible for the lawful basis, transparency to data subjects, authority to act for issuer companies and accuracy of submitted data. It must configure permissions, protect credentials, verify email and webhook destinations and respond to data-subject requests under its responsibility. If acting for another controller, it must ensure its instructions and this engagement are authorized by that controller.

s6.title: 6. Confidentiality and security
s6.content: Greenflow will limit access to those who need to process data to provide the Service and require confidentiality duties. It will maintain technical and organizational measures appropriate to the processing, including access controls, workspace and environment separation, API-key hashes, encryption of stored certificates and signed webhooks. Customers must also secure their own integrations.

s7.title: 7. Subprocessors and recipients
s7.content: The customer authorizes providers needed for infrastructure, storage, email, monitoring and support, subject to data-protection obligations appropriate to the service provided. Information about these providers may be requested through the privacy contact. Material changes affecting processing will be communicated where applicable, and the customer may submit a reasoned objection for assessment. Tax authorities receive data for their statutory responsibilities; they are not automatically Greenflow’s subprocessors. Customers define email and webhook destinations.

s8.title: 8. Assistance and incidents
s8.content: Considering the nature of processing and available information, Greenflow will provide reasonable assistance with data-subject rights, risk assessment and data-protection obligations. Upon becoming aware of an incident affecting personal data processed on the customer’s behalf, it will notify the customer without undue delay with available information and necessary updates. The controller remains responsible for assessing and making notifications to the authority and data subjects within statutory deadlines, without excluding Greenflow’s own obligations.

s9.title: 9. Return, deletion and retention
s9.content: Upon Service termination, the customer may request access, export or deletion of personal data under its responsibility through the privacy contact. Greenflow will comply with lawful instructions under contracted conditions and applicable law. Data requiring retention on a lawful basis will have access restricted to the corresponding purpose; backup deletion will follow the maintenance cycle and applicable obligations. The customer must retain copies of fiscal documents required for its activity. Account closure does not cancel documents with the tax authority.

s10.title: 10. International transfers and contact
s10.content: Where processing involves an international transfer, the parties must follow the mechanisms and safeguards required by the LGPD and applicable regulations. This Addendum alone does not replace standard contractual clauses or another instrument required for a specific transfer. Send requests about instructions, providers, security measures or transfers to legal@corvo.tech.
